title.narrative: Regional Project on Takaful for Resilience and Financial Inclusion in the Arab States

description.narrative: In recent years, inclusive insurance - including Shariah-compliant Takaful - has emerged as an important enabler of economic resilience, social protection, and financial inclusion across the Arab States. By pooling risks and providing affordable protection against shocks, Takaful can help households, micro and small enterprises, and farmers manage climate, health, and economic risks, while supporting livelihoods and entrepreneurship. Yet insurance penetration in most Arab States remains among the lowest globally, generally below 2 per cent of GDP. These gaps reflect structural economic and fiscal constraints, high informality, persistent gender inequalities, and elevated exposure to conflict, climate, and disaster risks. Despite growing policy recognition of Takaful’s potential within national financial inclusion and resilience agendas, the mentioned gaps persist due to fragmented regulatory frameworks, weak market infrastructure, and limited capacity to translate policy ambition into accessible, gender-responsive insurance coverage at scale. To address these gaps, UNDP is advancing a Regional Takaful and Inclusive Insurance Initiative, led by UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Arab States as part of its Regional Programme. The initiative acts as a catalytic platform to strengthen inclusive insurance ecosystems and expand access to Shariah-compliant risk protection by supporting policy and regulatory reforms, building supervisory and institutional capacity, and fostering innovation in insurance products and delivery models. Anchored in national priorities and aligned with financial inclusion, climate resilience, and social protection frameworks, the initiative places strong emphasis on gender equality and women’s economic empowerment.
